title: Empirical Comparison: Quick Scan (Static) vs. Deep Scan (Dynamic)

key_findings.summary: Quick Scan is ~200x faster, enabling inline browser link interception without user friction.

key_findings.quick_scan: CPU: ~0.1% / Scan; Memory: stateless / in-memory cache
key_findings.deep_scan: Container: 512MB RAM, Playwright Chromium headless process
key_findings.summary: Quick Scan scales horizontally with zero container overhead; Deep Scan requires strict egress controls and authorization.

key_findings.quick_scan_detection: Detects shorteners and redirect query tokens as weak signals; cannot follow hops without SSRF risk
key_findings.deep_scan_detection: Follows HTTP 301/302 hops inside egress-firewalled container; catches deceptive multi-hop landing pages
key_findings.recommendation: Use Quick Scan for instantaneous pre-flight check, escalating to Deep Scan when redirect token or shortener is detected.

key_findings.quick_scan_detection: Static lexical matching of 'login', 'verify' tokens, brand subdomains, and suspicious paths
key_findings.deep_scan_detection: Inspects rendered DOM, password inputs, and form action destination cross-origin targets
key_findings.recommendation: Deep Scan confirms zero-hour credential phishing pages that use benign-looking random domain names.

tactical_guideline: Quick Scan remains the default operational mode for high throughput. Deep Scan is isolated to restricted sandbox execution only upon explicit user request or elevated threat triage.
